newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik govt brings fighters close to rebel base.
newsitem.headline: Tajik govt brings fighters close to rebel base.

text.p: The Tajik government flew 40 rebel fighters from Afghanistan to Tajikistan on Thursday as it struggled to meet a 4 p.m. (1100 GMT) deadline from a rebel group holding more than a dozen Russian and Western hostages.

Government spokesman Zafar Saidov said helicopters carrying the 40 fighters had landed near Obigarm, 80 km (50 miles) east of the capital Dushanbe, where fighters Rizvon and Bakhron Sadirov are holding their captives.
"The government side has already informed Rizvon and Bakhron about the location of the helicopter," Saidov said. "The fighters will soon be brought to the exchange point."
Bakhrom Sadirov, who seized his first hostages more than a week ago, had demanded that the government bring the fighters to join his group.

His fighters said in a statement released through the United Nations Dushanbe office that they would free five captives unliaterally on Thursday, but that Bakhrom would step up his demands unless a previous ultimatum was met.

"Commander Bakhrom has shown remarkable patience which proves his positive attitude; however, should the Tajik government delay the ultimatum given, he would be forced to set a new ultimatum," the message said.

Four U.N. military observers, four Russian reporters and four workers with the United Nations refugee agency are among the captives. The rebels also seized Tajikistan's Security Minister on Saturday when he flew in to negotiate.
There have been a series of announcements that the hostages would be released, but none has been fulfilled.

The Tajik government is struggling to assert its authority against armed groups across the mountainous impoverished former Soviet republic. Many Islamic fighters -- like the rest of Sadirov's group -- are based in neighbouring Afghanistan.
The authorities sent helicopters to Afghanistan to pick up Sadirov's 40 fighters on Wednesday, but government officials said the return flight had been delayed for technical reasons.
The hostage crisis comes as the government and the opposition rebels are trying to end a bitter four-year civil war that has left tens of thousands dead and many more homeless.
A ceasefire agreed at a meeting in northern Afghanistan last December appears to be holding.
